Maya: Hey — quick one: swapped to a Windows dev box and my SDK calls keep 401. Same env file works on mac. Anyone run into .env/newline/encoding weirdness with Basic auth headers?
Ravi: can you paste how you're constructing the header and the .env line?
Maya: sure. .env has `REDFWD_API_KEY=abcd1234` (no quotes). Code is basically:```js
const key = process.env.REDFWD_API_KEY;
const header = 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(`${key}:`).toString('base64');
fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: header } });
```
Maya: on mac this works. on Windows get 401. :confused:
Sam: two quick things: 1) windows editors can leave a trailing `\r` (CRLF) in the env var; 2) some shells export with quotes. Try logging `JSON.stringify(key)` to see invisible chars.
Lena: also check BOM (UTF-8 BOM at start) and make sure dotenv lib is trimming. Which dotenv lib/version?
Maya: using dotenv 10.0.0 via node 18. Logging shows "abcd1234\r" (ugh).
Ravi: there you go. The `\r` will be part of the base64 payload, so server decodes and gets "abcd1234\r:" which doesn't match. Quick fix: `const key = process.env.REDFWD_API_KEY?.trim()`
Sam: yep. Another trick for curl testing: `curl -u "$REDFWD_API_KEY:" https://api.redwood.inference/...` — note the trailing colon is important when using only api-key as username.
Maya: interesting — I assumed `-u $KEY` would do it but that treats it differently. Good call.
Lena: also, when setting env in PowerShell people sometimes do `setx REDFWD_API_KEY "abcd..."` which persists quotes. In PowerShell use `setx REDFWD_API_KEY abcd1234` (no quotes) or trim after reading.
Maya: for posterity, here's a small checklist I used: 
• `node -e "console.log(JSON.stringify(process.env.REDFWD_API_KEY))"` to spot `\r` or quotes
• `type .env | sed -n '1p' | od -c` (WSL/git-bash) to inspect bytes
• add `.trim()` on read or sanitize at process-start

devx-bot: Docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/devex/auth#basic-auth (see "API key as username" section) :book:
Ravi: another gotcha — some SDK wrappers accidentally re-encode header if you pass username/password vs Authorization header string. If you're using a client helper, check it doesn't do `btoa` again.
Sam: tl;dr: include the colon when you base64 encode (i.e. `base64(api_key + ':')`), strip CRLF/BOM/quotes from env, and prefer explicit `Authorization` header if wrapper behavior is unclear. :thumbsup:
Maya: fixed by trimming + re-exporting without quotes. Thanks everyone, leaving this thread for future search. :raised_hands:
